polityNote: Portuguese Mozambique (overseas province) from the district reform of 1954-10-20 to independence; the units are the colonial distritos (9, then 10 from 1970-08-05). Atoms: geoBoundaries MOZ ADM2 (INE / OCHA ROSEA 2019, 159 districts incl. the city districts and Lago Niassa, CC BY 3.0 IGO). Province/district = union of present districts (gb ADM1 is OSM/Wambacher and does not nest; membership is INE’s, the best ADM1 overlap of every district agrees). Two gb atoms (Ilha Licom = Likoma, Ilha Risunodo = Chizumulu) are Malawian islands and are named outside. Each district is the union of the present districts of its successor province: statoids lists no boundary change between 1954 and independence other than the 1970 split of Manica e Sofala and the 1975 transfer of Tambara and Guro, both of which follow present district lines. The lake sector off Niassa became Portuguese by the 1954 Anglo-Portuguese agreement, whose day relative to the reform is not established.
